about.title: Colusa Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Colusa is a small, tight-knit community along Rt 20, and residents here rely on everyday products — farm equipment, tools, appliances, vehicle parts — just like anywhere else. When one of those products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the harm can be sudden and serious. California law generally lets an injured person pursue a strict liability claim, meaning you typically don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. That legal framework can help Colusa County residents move a claim forward even against companies with no local presence. We evaluate what happened, help preserve the product as evidence, and explain how manufacturers, distributors, and sellers may share responsibility. There's no obligation to move forward, and we work on contingency — no fee unless you recover.

items.title: Strict Liability Means You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: California generally allows injured people to hold manufacturers responsible by showing a defect caused harm, without needing to prove carelessness in how the product was made.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers may all be liable for a defective product, which can open more than one path toward accountability for what happened.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters Early On
items.desc: Our team can advise you on keeping the product and packaging intact, since physical evidence is often central to proving a design, manufacturing, or warning defect.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the company was careless. Our team can review your situation and explain how this applies to your specific claim.

items.question: I live in a small town like Colusa — can I still bring a claim against a large manufacturer?
items.answer: Yes. Where you live doesn't limit your right to pursue a claim against a manufacturer, distributor, or retailer based elsewhere. Colusa County residents have the same legal standing under California law as anyone else in the state.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try not to discard, repair, or alter it, since the product itself is often the most important evidence in these cases. Our team can advise you on how to preserve it properly while your claim is evaluated.
